title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 1

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the handover exercise begin?
tasks.audioText: The maintenance team will practise a shift handover briefing on Wednesday at seven forty-five. Students should meet in the planning room and bring the sample task-status board. The briefing will cover completed work, outstanding tasks, parts awaiting confirmation and issues that require follow-up. The tutor will assess whether the information is concise and unambiguous.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which board should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The maintenance team will practise a shift handover briefing on Wednesday at seven forty-five. Students should meet in the planning room and bring the sample task-status board. The briefing will cover completed work, outstanding tasks, parts awaiting confirmation and issues that require follow-up. The tutor will assess whether the information is concise and unambiguous.

tasks.prompt: A useful handover summarises the status of work at the end of a shift. It identifies completed tasks, outstanding items, relevant references and any issue that requires attention. Unconfirmed information should be clearly labelled as such. The incoming team should be able to distinguish between work that has been completed, work that remains open and decisions that still require approval. Reading 1. What should a useful handover identify?
options: Only the names of the team members
The cost of the next maintenance visit
Completed tasks, outstanding items, references and issues requiring attention
The personal opinions of the outgoing team

tasks.prompt: Why should unconfirmed information be labelled?
options: So that the report can be made longer
Because all information must be treated as final
To avoid recording who supplied the information
So the incoming team can distinguish facts from information still awaiting confirmation

tasks.prompt: Outstanding tasks ___ clearly in the handover record.
Choose TWO elements of a reliable maintenance handover.
A formal transfer of work information between teams or shifts is a ___.
A task remains incomplete at the end of the shift. What should you say?
options: The task is finished even though it is not.
The task remains open; the reference and required follow-up are recorded here.
The next team can guess what happened.
There is no need to mention it.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of maintenance handover in a logical order.
options: Brief the incoming team and record follow-up
correctOrder: Brief the incoming team and record follow-up

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words for a maintenance handover. Summarise completed work, outstanding tasks and one issue that needs confirmation.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Handover content — 2: accurately summarises completed work, outstanding tasks and the issue requiring confirmation; 1: covers two elements; 0: incomplete or inaccurate. (2) Status and follow-up — 2: identifies task status, next action and responsible role without implying unapproved completion; 1: partial; 0: absent. (3) Record integrity — 2: explains that relevant controlled records and required sign-off must remain current; 1: partial; 0: absent or incorrect. (4) English — 2: concise, logically organised handover language and accurate technical vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
